case.case_title: Samanthilaka v. Ernest Perera and Others
case.source_citation: Sri Lanka Law Reports [1990] 1 Sri L.R. 318

clause.text: Any person detained shall be brought before a judge and cannot be held without legal order.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioner was detained without being produced before a judge as required by Article 13(2), constituting a violation of her fundamental rights.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed she was detained by police officers without being produced before a judge or any legal authority, violating her right to personal liberty under Article 13(2).
case_context.respondent_argument: Respondents argued procedural defects in the petition and questioned the necessity of naming individual officers, but did not dispute the legal requirement of production before a judge.
key_facts: Petitioner was held in police custody without being produced before a judge.
Petitioner was subjected to interrogation and assault during detention.
Petitioner’s family was denied access during detention.
Petitioner was a minor and faced difficulties in gathering evidence.
Respondents challenged procedural aspects but did not deny the legal standard.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The Court interpreted Article 13(2) as requiring that any person detained must be brought before a judge promptly and held only under a legal order. The Court emphasized the State’s liability for violations by its agents and rejected the argument that failure to name individual officers was fatal.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The Court found that the petitioner was detained without being produced before a judge and was held unlawfully, thus violating Article 13(2). The evidence showed police officers acted under color of office in breaching this constitutional right.
principles_established: Detention without production before a judge is unlawful under Article 13(2).
State liability arises from executive or administrative action violating fundamental rights.
Procedural defects in naming respondents do not bar relief if violation is established.
precedents_cited: Saman v. Leeladasa and Another [1989] 1 Sri LR 1
Mariadas Raj v. Attorney-General and Others [1982] FRD 397
Ganeshanathan v. Vivienne Goonewardene and Another [1984] 1 Sri LR 319

outcome.holding: The Court held that the petitioner was detained without being produced before a judge and thus her rights under Article 13(2) were violated, entitling her to a declaration of violation.
outcome.remedy_or_orders: Declaration of violation of Article 13(2); compensation and costs as ordered.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 13(2) was central to the Court’s finding that the petitioner’s detention was unlawful due to failure to produce her before a judge, directly supporting the relief granted.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The petitioner was held in police custody without being produced before a judge and was denied access to her parents, as supported by affidavits and the Medico-Legal Report.
